label: thm:summary
statement_latex: \label{thm:summary} For complex square matrices the following statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item A linear space is level precisely when all its positive-degree rook numbers vanish. Equivalently, its first $n$ rook cumulants vanish. \item The cumulants have the connected-partition formula of Theorem~\ref{thm:connected}. On doubly centred matrices the degree-five and degree-six expansions are exactly those in Table~\ref{tab:cumulants}. \item For $n\geq2$, \[ 2n-3\leq\LS(n)\leq \min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac{n^2-1}{2}\right\rfloor, \left\lfloor\frac{n^2+2n-1}{3}\right\rfloor\right\}. \] A real level space has dimension at most $2n-2$. \item The function $\LS$ is superadditive, and \[ \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\LS(n)}n =\sup_{n\geq1}\frac{\LS(n)}n, \] where infinity is permitted. \end{enumerate}

label: thm:symmetric-summary
title: Symmetric spaces and the Klein slice
statement_latex: \label{thm:symmetric-summary} Every complex level space of six-by-six matrices invariant under a full row or column six-cycle has dimension at most ten. The same bound holds if a nonidentity scalar $\omega\ne1$ is the action on the whole space of a row permutation, column permutation, or a composition of these with transposition. For every $p,q\ge2$, the standard level space supported in the first row and column, of dimension $p+q-3$, admits no proper linear level-space extension. Let $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb F_7)$ act simultaneously on the rows and columns indexed by $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_7)$. Each of its two conjugate non-real three-dimensional matrix summands has exactly twenty-four level lines, the cone over the ordinary flexes of Klein's quartic. Their direct sum contains no level space of dimension three, and a level space containing one of these pure lines has dimension one. The existence of a level plane transverse to both summands is not decided.

label: prop:barrier
statement_latex: \label{prop:barrier} Let $q\mid r\leq n$ and let $\omega$ be a primitive $q$th root of unity. Form matrices with $r/q$ independent row blocks $(a,\omega a,\ldots,\omega^{q-1}a)$ and all remaining rows zero. This is a space of dimension $nr/q$, and $S_k$ vanishes on it unless $q\mid k\leq r$. Let $C\ge0$. If vanishing in a set of orders $\Omega\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ forces every subspace to have dimension at most $Cn$, put $a=\lfloor C\rfloor+1$. Then for every $1\leq q\leq\lfloor n/a\rfloor$, $\Omega$ meets $\{q,2q,\ldots,aq\}$. In particular \[ |\Omega|\geq\left\lceil\frac{\lfloor n/a\rfloor}{a}\right\rceil, \qquad\max\Omega\geq\lfloor n/a\rfloor. \]

title: A shared bilinear two-level class
statement_latex: Suppose a binary monotone circuit has the following form: \begin{enumerate} \item Its first product gates are $R_i=A_i(X)B_i(Y)$, with pure-side linear disjunction operands, shared arbitrarily. \item Its second product gates multiply two disjunctions of the $R_i$. \item Its output is a disjunction of first and second product gates. \end{enumerate} All disjunction networks may have arbitrary fanout and sharing. For every unsafe rectangle put \[ U_i=\{x\in A_i:B_i\subseteq N(x)\}. \] If $|U_i|\leq1$ for every unsafe rectangle, the circuit can be replaced without growth by a quadratic circuit with edge support $E$. label: thm:four-summary
title: The four-witness reductions
statement_latex: \label{thm:four-summary} Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with no four-cycle and let a positive variable-input binary circuit $C$ compute $P\in\Sup(G)$ with nonempty quadratic support $H$. If eight vertices induce four disjoint edges in $G$ and no edge in $H$, at least four product gates are deleted in forming $C_2$. If $|E(G)\setminus E(H)|=4$ and $|C|<|E(G)|+\tau(G)-1$, the only remaining numerical possibilities are \[ \begin{array}{c|l} d&(D,e)\\\hline 2&(5,0)\\ 3&(5,0),(5,1),(6,0). \end{array} \] In particular, every circuit with four missing witnesses and cover gain four satisfies the full star lower bound. More generally, if the four missing edges form an induced matching and six gates are deleted, four of them products, then $\tau(G)\le K+2$, where $K$ is the number of products in $C_2$; this again implies the full star lower bound. In the row $(d,D,e)=(3,5,0)$, the missing-edge graph cannot be $P_4\sqcup K_2$ or $K_3\sqcup K_2$, where $P_4$ denotes the path with three edges. If $G$ has girth at least five, the shape $P_4\sqcup K_2$ is also excluded in the row $(d,D,e)=(3,6,0)$; hence that shape satisfies the full bound at cover gain three whenever its quadratic frame is optimal.

label: thm:intro-second
title: The second height stratum
statement_latex: \label{thm:intro-second} Fix a prime $p$ and use the counting hypersurface $X_\Phi$ defined in Section~\ref{sec:construction}. If $p\mid S$, then $p\mid T_{p+1}(\Phi)$ and \[ h(X_\Phi)=2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T_{p+1}(\Phi)/p\not\equiv0\pmod p. \] More precisely, simultaneous rotation of the first $p$ positions in all the lists counted by $T_{p+1}$, leaving the last position fixed, has $S^2$ fixed points. If $O_p(\Phi)$ is the number of its nontrivial orbits, then \[ T_{p+1}(\Phi)=S^2+pO_p(\Phi),\qquad h(X_\Phi)=2\Longleftrightarrow O_p(\Phi)\not\equiv0\pmod p. \] For fixed $p$, $O_p$ is a $\#\mathrm P$ function. Deciding height two on the promise $p\mid S$ is $\mathrm{Mod}_p\mathrm P$-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. For every prime, two logically equivalent formulas with equal exact satisfying count, and with the same hypersurface degree, can have height two and height at least three, respectively.

label: thm:intro-points
title: A point-count criterion
statement_latex: \label{thm:intro-points} Let $X\subset\mathbb P^{d-1}_{\mathbb F_p}$ be smooth and geometrically integral of degree $d\ge4$, and assume its top Artin--Mazur height is at least two. Put $n=d-2$, $N_r=\#X(\mathbb F_{p^r})$, and $\tau_r=(-1)^n(N_r-\sum_{i=0}^n p^{ir})$. Then \[ h(X)=2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v_p\!\left(\frac{\tau_1^2-\tau_2}{2}\right)=1. \] For odd $p$ this is equivalent to $\tau_2/p\not\equiv0\pmod p$, so $N_2\bmod p^2$ suffices. For $p=2$ it is equivalent to $(\tau_1^2-\tau_2)/4\not\equiv0\pmod2$, determined by $N_1\bmod4$ and $N_2\bmod8$. There exist smooth quintic threefolds with identical $N_1$ and identical $N_2\bmod4$ but different height-two status.

label: thm:intro-complexity
title: Exact height and its complexity
statement_latex: \label{thm:intro-complexity} Let $F$ be a division-free arithmetic circuit over $\mathbb F_p$, with its $d\ge3$ variables explicitly listed, promised to represent a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$ defining a smooth hypersurface $X\subset\mathbb P^{d-1}$. For a homogeneous integral lift put \[ a_{p^j}=[(x_1\cdots x_d)^{p^j-1}]\widetilde F^{p^j-1},\qquad B_d=\begin{cases}2,&d=3,\\36,&d=4,\\ \binom{2d-1}{d-1},&d\ge5.\end{cases} \] The first index $j\le B_d$ with $a_{p^j}\not\equiv0\pmod{p^j}$ is $h(X)$. If there is no such index, then $h(X)=\infty$. For every fixed prime $p$ and fixed positive integer $r$, deciding $h(X)=r$ belongs to $\mathrm{Mod}_p\mathrm P$. The same membership holds with $r$ supplied in unary and allowed to grow with the input; the resulting variable-$r$ problem is complete. The cases $r=1,2$ are complete for that class, and at $p=2$ the case $r=3$ is $\oplus\mathrm P$-complete even under the promise $h(X)\ge3$. The exact-height function, including the output $\infty$, is computable deterministically with $\operatorname{poly}(L)$ work bits, where $L$ is the circuit input length, and therefore in $2^{\operatorname{poly}(L)}$ time. This upper bound also permits a binary-encoded input prime. A separate dense implementation uses $2^{O(d\log p)}\operatorname{poly}(s,d,\log p)$ bit operations, where $s$ is circuit size. Under this uniform convention the function is $\#\mathrm P$-hard by polynomially many nonadaptive oracle calls, even on inputs of height at least two. With a unary-encoded prime, promised height-two decision is oracle-equivalent to exact counting as stated in Theorem~\ref{thm:uniform-counting}. The same oracle equivalence holds for arbitrary unary requested heights, as in Theorem~\ref{thm:unary-height}.

title: Point-count test on the Hasse-zero locus

label: thm:maximal-odd-affine;eq:odd-family-count
title: Classification and exact number
statement_latex: \label{thm:maximal-odd-affine} A nonempty affine family \(A=\theta+W\subseteq\Theta(C)\) consists of odd theta characteristics precisely when \(\epsilon(\theta)=1\) and \(q_\theta|_W=0\). Every inclusion-maximal such family has dimension \(g-1\), and hence cardinality \(2^{g-1}\). Moreover: \begin{enumerate} \item Every \((g-1)\)-dimensional \(B\)-isotropic subspace \(W\subset V\) is the direction of exactly one maximal odd affine family. \item These families form a single orbit under the natural symplectic action on quadratic refinements. \item Their number is \begin{equation} M_g=(2^g-1)\prod_{j=2}^g(2^j+1). \label{eq:odd-family-count} \end{equation} Each odd theta characteristic lies in exactly \(\prod_{j=2}^g(2^j+1)\) such families. \end{enumerate} Consequently, for \(g=2k\) the maximum dimension is \(2k-1\), the maximum cardinality is \(2^{2k-1}\), and the minimum ambient codimension is \(2k+1\).

label: thm:unary-height
title: Unary height decisions
statement_latex: \label{thm:unary-height} Fix a prime $p$. On the smooth homogeneous circuit inputs specified above, with a positive integer $r$ supplied in unary, deciding $h(X)=r$ is $\mathrm{Mod}_p\mathrm P$-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. Then $H_{\mathrm{unary}}\in\mathrm P^{\#\mathrm P}$, using one exact counting query followed by a remainder computation. With promise-respecting oracle calls, \[ \mathrm{FP}^{H_{\mathrm{unary}}}=\mathrm{FP}^{\#\mathrm P}. \]

label: thm:uniform-counting
title: Uniform height two and exact counting
statement_latex: \label{thm:uniform-counting} Let $\mathcal H_2$ be the promise decision problem whose input is a prime $p$ in unary and a width-three formula $\Phi$, promised to have $p\mid\#\operatorname{SAT}(\Phi)$, and whose answer is whether the counting hypersurface $X_\Phi$ has height two.
